# Evaluation scorecard

<!-- Generated by sifted_eval (eval/sifted_eval.cpp). Do not edit by hand. -->

How accurately and robustly Sifted tracks, scored against simulator ground truth over every scenario fixture, under network impairment and sensor faults. All numbers on this page come from one command (run from the repository root):

```bash
cmake --preset release && cmake --build --preset release
build/release/eval/sifted_eval --out docs/evaluation.md
```

The tool, the regression tests and the degraded-network and fault tests share one implementation of loading, scoring and the conditions (`eval/sifted/eval/`); a test (`Eval.*` in `tests/eval_test.cpp`) checks that the tool's direct-feed numbers equal the regression baselines. Accuracy does not depend on CPU speed, load or timing: the inputs are recorded fixtures, time is an input, the impairment model is seeded, and the engine is a deterministic function of its ordered input (docs/design.md section 3). Running the command twice gives a byte-identical file, and any machine with the same compiler and maths library gives the same numbers.

Estimator: `imm` (EngineConfig::motion_model; ADR 0014). The legacy constant-velocity filter against the IMM, including manoeuvres beyond these fixtures: [motion-model-evaluation.md](motion-model-evaluation.md).

This page is the fast regression scorecard: one sensor-noise realisation per scenario (the seeds vary only the network), so a zero here can be the luck of one draw. The statistical evaluation over hundreds of independent noise realisations, with intervals, GOSPA and a clutter and detection sweep, is [evaluation-monte-carlo.md](evaluation-monte-carlo.md); the comparison with an external Stone Soup baseline on the same runs and scorer is [evaluation-baseline.md](evaluation-baseline.md).

Scenarios: `close_pass`, `crossing_pair`, `demo`, `enter_leave`, `formation_split`, `straight_crossing`, `turn`. Seeds: 7, 8, 9. Reorder windows: 0.50 s (the daemon uses 0.50 s).

## Summary over all scenarios

Each row merges every scenario and seed of one condition (runs = scenarios x seeds). ## Filter consistency (direct engine feed)

Average NEES (4-dof full state, 2-dof position) over the RMSE's samples, split into estimates at their own update instant ("upd.") and extrapolated or coasting ones ("extr."), and average NIS per sensor kind; a consistent filter averages the degrees of freedom. The bracket is the 95% interval for the updated NEES4 under independence, which these time-correlated samples do not satisfy: a guide, not a test (docs/design.md section 7).

## Conditions

- **direct**: the scenario's frames, decoded by the real decoder, fed to the engine scan by scan (`run_engine`). The regression tests' path.
- **pipeline conditions** (every other row): frames sent at their measurement time through the seeded impairment model (ADR 0008), then fed to `net::Pipeline` exactly as the daemon consumes them: arrival order, receive time = arrival time, a quiet tick after 100 ms (`run_pipeline`). Truth instant T is scored on the tracks the pipeline holds at T, extrapolated to T, so even a clean network scores slightly worse than the direct feed: the scan stamped T is still being assembled.
- **clean**: no loss, delay, jitter or duplication.
- **mild**: 1% loss, delay 20 ms + U(0, 50 ms), 1% duplicated.
- **moderate**: 3% loss + Gilbert-Elliott bursts (good->bad 0.01, bad->good 0.25, 60% loss when bad), delay 50 ms + U(0, 400 ms), 2% duplicated.
- **severe**: 8% loss + Gilbert-Elliott bursts (good->bad 0.03, bad->good 0.20, 80% loss when bad), delay 100 ms + U(0, 800 ms), 5% duplicated.
- **mild + N s outage**: every link down for N s, from 30 s after the first truth instant, on the mild level.
- **clean + range-bearing dropout 6 s**: the first range-bearing sensor of the table sends nothing for 6 s from 30 s after the first truth instant; every other sensor untouched (`eval/sifted/eval/conditions.cpp`).
- **clean + bearing-only intermittent**: the first bearing-only sensor of the table is switched off for whole 2 s periods, each with probability 0.4 (seed 17); every other sensor untouched (`eval/sifted/eval/conditions.cpp`).

A link with nothing random in it gives the same arrivals for every seed, so those conditions run once per window. Conditions that need a sensor kind a scenario lacks are left out for it.

## Metric definitions

CLEAR-MOT style (Bernardin and Stiefelhagen, 2008); the authoritative definitions are in `eval/sifted/eval/scenario.hpp`. At each truth time T, once the tracker has consumed its input up to T:

- **Reported tracks** are the confirmed and coasting tracks, extrapolated to T. They are matched one-to-one to the truth targets present at T: a target's previous match is kept while that track is still reported and within 100 m; the rest are matched by a minimum-total-distance assignment with pairs further apart than 100 m forbidden. The matcher knows nothing about which track "should" be which target.
- **RMSE** (position, per target): over covered, matched instants at least 10 s after the target first enters coverage. Mean RMSE averages the targets; worst RMSE is the largest.
- **Missed**: covered targets unmatched at least 5 s after they first enter coverage, out of all such (eligible) target-instants.
- **ID switches**: a target matched to a different track than the last time it was matched.
- **False tracks**: reported tracks matched to any target (covered or not) in fewer than half of the instants they were reported.
- **Recovery** after an outage or fault window [start, end): the targets covered and matched at the last truth instant before start and still covered after end; a target has recovered at the first instant >= end at which it is matched to a track updated after end (extrapolation through the gap does not count). Recovery time runs from end until all have recovered; "survived" counts targets still on the track they had before. Mean and worst are over the runs that recovered; "never" counts runs that did not within the scenario.
- **NEES** e^T P^-1 e of the estimate against truth and **NIS** y^T S^-1 y (the engine's own gating distance of every associated update on a matched track), as in `eval/sifted/eval/consistency.hpp`.
